scenario: Assay labs report rare-earth oxide (REO) concentrations only when they exceed the 0.60% instrument sensitivity floor. Among reported assays the mean REO concentration is 0.85% (σ=0.15%). The true mean concentration across all drill samples is of interest.

data.description: Observed statistics among units exceeding reporting threshold

values.n_observed: only values above threshold are recorded

question: (a) Assuming the true distribution of REO concentration is normal with σ=0.15 %, solve for the true population mean μ such that E[X|X>0.6]=0.85. (b) What fraction of all events lie above the above 0.60% assay-sensitivity floor threshold? (c) By how much does the observed mean overstate the true mean?

ground_truth.explanation: Solving the truncated-normal equation μ + σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ) = 0.85 numerically gives μ≈0.83038. Only 93.8% of all events are actually observed; the observed mean overstates the true mean by ≈0.0196 %.

naive_answer: The true mean REO concentration is approximately 0.85 % because that is what the data directly show.
naive_trap: The observed mean is a truncated-normal conditional expectation, not the population mean; it always exceeds the true mean for above-threshold samples.
reasoning_trace: (1) Let α=(t−μ)/σ. (2) E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 0.85 and solve numerically for μ using brentq. (4) Solution: μ≈0.83038. (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((0.6−0.83038)/σ)≈0.93771.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 0.85,0.15,0.6
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-20*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=200)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-0.83038)<0.005
assert abs(frac-0.93771)<0.005
assert mu_sol < obs
